about.title: Personal Injury Help in Oroville, California
about.longDescription: Oroville is a tight-knit Butte County community of about 16,260 people, but its roads still see their share of collisions. In the most recent reporting year, Oroville logged 102 injury collisions with 145 people hurt and 2 traffic deaths. Corridors like Oroville Dam Boulevard East, Oroville Dam Boulevard West, Olive Highway, and Feather River Boulevard carry a large share of the city's daily traffic, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. when commuters, students, and shoppers overlap. If you or someone you love was hurt in a crash, a fall, or another accident caused by someone else's carelessness, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and paperwork can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. We listen to what happened and help you evaluate your situation. There's no cost to reach out, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. Getting informed early, especially with California's filing deadlines, can make a real difference in your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the accident, and claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Sharing Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault. We can help sort out how fault gets divided.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit the non-economic damages you can pursue, such as pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't automatically capped just because your injuries are hard to put a price on.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover Something
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you don't pay out of pocket to have your case reviewed or handled. Fees only come out of an eventual settlement or award, not upfront.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. There's no cost to reach out and discuss your situation. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. If a government entity is involved, such as a city road department, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth getting informed early.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, rather than being eliminated entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Oroville?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, corridors such as Oroville Dam Boulevard East, Oroville Dam Boulevard West, Olive Highway, and Feather River Boulevard show higher volumes of reported crashes, with activity often peaking on Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much compensation I can receive?
items.answer: For ordinary personal injury cases in California, there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This differs from certain other types of claims, so we can walk you through what applies to your specific situation.
